findings.reason: the section's write path omits the module the fix must edit, so the node either edits outside its scope or returns blocked.
findings.text: §4 says "The commit-list check in `reckon/crew/promotion.py`", but `promotion.py` only unpacks the value (`promotion.py:527`, `promotion.py:670`); the subset test that produced the 16-of-17 shortfall is `_require_gate_evidence` in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:~908` (`resolving_presented < resolving_declared`), and the presented-citation and commitless-beyond-base refusals are `_require_commits_beyond_base` in the same file, so a worker scoped to `promotion.py` + the new test would find no commit-list check to change

findings.reason: the mechanism cannot be implemented where the plan puts it, and the caller the plan relies on is never named.
findings.text: §3 says `crew complete` builds the gate check from the run's stored review record, but the point where a passing gate's check is filled is `_default_gate_evidence_from_manifest` in `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:244`, called at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:357`; `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py` holds only `_require_gate_check_precondition` (line 1323), which receives `gate_check`, `gate` and `require_gate_check` and neither the run record nor the run's role, so the declared write path cannot reach the record

findings.reason: without its own case the worker can drop that deliverable and still pass every stated case, so the plan would certify work it did not get.
findings.text: §2 promises that "a bare name that matches more than one head id covers all of them, and the promotion record names that it did", but §2's done-when (lines 52-57) tests only the promoting case, the one-uncovered-id refusal and the cross-file non-cover case, so the multi-match behaviour and the record annotation ship unmeasured

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §4 names `reckon/crew/promotion.py` as the home of the commit-list check, and that module only re-binds the returned `commit_list_shortfall` value; the check is `_require_gate_evidence` in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's third deliverable bullet (a bare name matching several head ids covers all of them and the record says so) has no case in §2's done-when.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the plan names no log path, so gate logs fall to the crew run directory, which is durable; the tests it names are new repository test files.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the three new test filenames name the mechanism (`test_a_red_base_matches_bare_names.py`, `test_a_review_run_gate_is_its_record.py`, `test_a_presented_head_covers_its_ancestors.py`) and carry no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 says `crew complete` builds the gate check from the stored review record, but the build point is `_default_gate_evidence_from_manifest` in `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py` (called from `reckon/crew/promotion.py:357`), outside the section's declared write path.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2, §3 and §4 names one check to repair, and the followup's single invocation covers all three only because they are disjoint files.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan declares no depends-on, informs or gates, and `plan-standalone` states the same ("no live plan waits on it and it waits on none"); the three open sections write disjoint files, as the followup says.
